text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is generally defined as a consistent reading of 130/80 mm Hg or higher.
Blood pressure is measured using two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): The pressure in your arteries when your heart contracts.
Diastolic (bottom number): The pressure in your arteries when your heart relaxes between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: According to guidelines from the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, blood pressure categories are broken down as follows:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 1 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic
Stage 2 Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): 140 mm Hg or higher systolic or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic
Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic
Elevated blood pressure is a warning sign that you are at risk of developing full hypertension unless you take steps to improve your habits.
Stage 1 hypertension typically leads a healthcare provider to recommend lifestyle modifications, and potentially medication if you have a high risk of heart disease or stroke.
Stage 2 hypertension usually requires a combination of prescribed blood pressure medications and lifestyle changes.

A reading over 180/120 mm Hg is a medical emergency. If your reading is this high, wait five minutes and test again. If it remains this high and you have symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, or vision changes, call 911 immediately. If you don't have symptoms, contact your doctor right away.
